test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 30 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which phenomenon, successfully explained by the universal law of gravitation, relies on the combined and differential gravitational attraction exerted by both the moon and the sun on the earth?

options.text: The decrease in the value of g from poles to equator
The motion of planets around the Sun
The centripetal force keeping the stone in a circular path

solution:
The correct answer is __**The occurrence of ocean tides**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Universal Law of Gravitation**, formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton** in **1687**, states that every object in the universe attracts every other object with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
• **Ocean tides** are the periodic rise and fall of the sea level. This phenomenon is a direct consequence of the **gravitational pull** exerted by both the **Moon** and the **Sun** on the **Earth**. ***Hence, the occurrence of ocean tides is the correct answer.***
 
• The Moon, being much closer to Earth than the Sun, exerts a stronger **tidal force**. This force is "differential" because the gravitational attraction is stronger on the side of the Earth facing the Moon than on the center or the far side, causing the water to bulge.
 
• The **Sun** also exerts gravitational attraction. When the **Sun, Moon, and Earth** are aligned (during **New Moon** and **Full Moon**), their combined forces create **Spring Tides**, which are exceptionally high.
 
• When the Sun and Moon are at **right angles** to each other relative to Earth, their gravitational forces partially counteract each other, resulting in **Neap Tides**, which have a lower tidal range.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Variation of 'g' (Option 1):**
 
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity (g)** is not constant everywhere on Earth. It is **maximum at the poles** and **minimum at the equator**.
 
• This variation occurs because the Earth is an **oblate spheroid** (bulged at the equator) and due to the **centrifugal force** generated by **Earth's rotation**. It does not rely on the Sun or Moon's combined attraction. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Motion of Planets (Option 2):**
 
 
• The **motion of planets around the Sun** is explained by the gravitational force providing the necessary **centripetal force** for orbital motion.
 
• While this is a triumph of the universal law of gravitation, it describes the attraction between **two bodies** (Sun and a planet) rather than the combined differential attraction of two external bodies on a third. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Centripetal Force (Option 4):**
 
 
• The **centripetal force** keeping a stone in a circular path when tied to a string is provided by **tension** in the string, not the gravitational attraction of the Sun or Moon.
 
• In a broader sense, gravity acts as a centripetal force for celestial bodies, but in the context of a "stone," it is a mechanical tension. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gravitational Constant (G):** The value of the universal gravitational constant is **6.674 x 10^-11 Nm²/kg²**. It remains the same throughout the universe.
 
• **Tidal Cycle:** Most coastal areas experience **two high tides** and **two low tides** every **24 hours and 50 minutes**. This is known as a **lunar day**.
 
• **Barycenter:** The Earth and Moon actually orbit around their common center of mass, called the **barycenter**, which is located inside the Earth but off-center. This orbital motion also contributes to the centrifugal force that creates the tide on the far side of the Earth.
 
• **Mass vs. Distance:** Although the **Sun** is about **27 million times** more massive than the Moon, it is **400 times** further away. Since the tidal force decreases with the **cube of the distance**, the Moon's effect on tides is about **2.2 times** stronger than the Sun's.
